paras.t: Ecce enim Deus noster quem colimus fide, spe, caritate, et actibus latriæ, cujus in ditione cuncta sunt posita, potest eripere nos de camino ignis ardentis, imo de omni persecutione : juxta illud Isaiæ : Quum transieris per aquas, tecum ero; et flamma non ardebit in te ; et de manibus tuis, o rex, liberare : quemadmodum in secunda Petri epistola habetur : Novit Deus pios de tentatione eripere. De quo omnipotente Domino in libro Job scribitur : Deus cujus iræ nemo resistere potest : quis restitit ei, et habuit pacem?
paras.en: [[3:17|For behold our God, whom we worship|Ecce enim Deus noster quem colimus]] by faith, hope, charity and acts of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], in whose power all things are set[[Esth 13:9||]], [[3:17|is able to save us from the furnace of burning fire|potest eripere nos de camino ignis ardentis]], nay, from every persecution, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 43:2|When thou shalt pass through the waters, I will be with thee|Quum transieris per aquas, tecum ero]]; [[Is 43:2|and the flames shall not burn in thee|et flamma non ardebit in te]]; [[3:17|and to deliver us out of thy hands, O king|et de manibus tuis, o rex, liberare]], as we have in the second epistle of Peter: [[2 Pet 2:9|The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly from temptation|Novit Deus pios de tentatione eripere]]. Of this almighty Lord it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist|Deus cujus iræ nemo resistere potest]]: [[Job 9:4|who hath resisted him, and hath had peace|quis restitit ei, et habuit pacem]]?

paras.t: Quod si noluerit nos a temporali hac occisione præservare : interdum enim Deus electos suos permittit ab impiis trucidari ad beatitudinis suæ augmentum, juxta illud ad Hebræos, Alii autem distenti sunt, non suscipientes redemptionem, ut meliorem invenirent resurrectionem ; notum sit tibi, rex, quia deos tuos non colimus, et statuam auream non adoramus : id est, parati sumus potius mori, quam contra legem patrum nostrorum idololatrare, justitiamque relinquere, certi quod si Deus permiserit corpora nostra occidi, animas non relinquet : juxta illud secundi Machabæorum, Parati sumus magis mori, quam patrias Dei leges prævaricari.
paras.en: [[3:18|But if he will not|Quod si noluerit]] preserve us from this temporal slaying (for God sometimes permits his elect to be slaughtered by the wicked for the increase of their beatitude, according to that to the Hebrews: [[Heb 11:35|But others were racked, not accepting deliverance, that they might find a better resurrection|Alii autem distenti sunt, non suscipientes redemptionem, ut meliorem invenirent resurrectionem]]), [[3:18|be it known to thee, O king, that we will not worship thy gods, nor adore the golden statue|notum sit tibi, rex, quia deos tuos non colimus, et statuam auream non adoramus]]: that is, we are ready rather to die than to commit idolatry against the law of our fathers and to forsake justice, being sure that if God permits our bodies to be slain, he will not forsake our souls; according to that of the second of Machabees: [[2 Mach 7:2|we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of God, received from our fathers|Parati sumus magis mori, quam patrias Dei leges prævaricari]].

paras.t: Tunc Nabuchodonosor repletus est furore, reputans se contemptum : quod superbia ferre non potest, cupiens magni pendi ; et adspectus faciei illius immutatus est super Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago : id est, cordis sui turbatio in vultu apparuit, præsertim in oculis, ubi passiones animæ magis citiusque resultant ; et viros istos, quos dudum favorabiliter adspicere consuevit, nunc furibundo vultu adspexit. Sic et Jacob in Genesi ait conjugibus suis : Video faciem patris vestri, quod non est circa me sicut heri et nudiustertius. Et præcepit ut succenderetur fornax : quæ, secundum Albertum, in campo parata fuit ; septuplum, id est septies plus, quam succendi consueverat : quasi et simplex et solitus ignis non sufficeret sanctos occidere, et ut eos magis terreret. Furor namque et ira quæ insaniæ proxima est, modum nescit tenere. Propter quod in Ecclesiaste legitur : Ne sis facilis ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit ; et alibi, Ira non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor.
paras.en: [[3:19|Then was Nabuchodonosor filled with fury|Tunc Nabuchodonosor repletus est furore]], thinking himself despised, which pride, desiring to be highly esteemed, cannot bear; [[3:19|and the countenance of his face was changed against Sidrach, Misach, and Abdenago|et adspectus faciei illius immutatus est super Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago]]: that is, the disturbance of his heart appeared in his face, especially in the eyes, where the passions of the soul are reflected more, and sooner; and these men, whom he had formerly been wont to look upon with favour, he now looked upon with a furious face. So too in Genesis Jacob says to his wives: [[Gen 31:5|I see your father's countenance is not towards me as yesterday and the other day|Video faciem patris vestri, quod non est circa me sicut heri et nudiustertius]]. [[3:19|and he commanded that the furnace should be heated|Et præcepit ut succenderetur fornax]], which, according to Albert, had been made ready in the plain, [[3:19|seven times more|septuplum]], that is, seven times over, [[3:19|than it had been accustomed to be heated|quam succendi consueverat]]: as though a simple and ordinary fire were not enough to kill the saints, and so that he might terrify them the more. For fury, and anger, which is very near to madness, knows not how to keep measure. Wherefore we read in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 7:10|Be not quickly angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of a fool|Ne sis facilis ad irascendum, quia ira in sinu stulti requiescit]]; and elsewhere: [[Prov 27:4|Anger hath no mercy: nor fury, when it breaketh forth|Ira non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor]].

paras.t: Et viris fortissimis corporali fortitudine de exercitu suo jussit, ut ligatis pedibus Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago, mitterent eos in fornacem ignis ardentis. Et quid necesse fuit pedes eorum ligari, nisi quod iræ impetus ratione non utitur?
paras.en: [[3:20|And he commanded the strongest men|Et viris fortissimis]], strongest in bodily strength, [[3:20|that were in his army|de exercitu suo jussit]], [[3:20|to bind the feet of Sidrach, Misach, and Abdenago, and to cast them into the furnace of burning fire|ut ligatis pedibus Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago, mitterent eos in fornacem ignis ardentis]]. And what need was there for their feet to be bound, except that the onrush of anger does not use reason?

paras.t: Et confestim viri illi tres vincti pedibus cum braccis : pro quo nomine Aquila et Theodotion sarabalia dixerunt, quæ hic sumuntur pro teguminibus crurum ac tibiarum, secundum Hieronymum et Albertum ; et tiaris. Tiara, secundum Hieronymum, Græcum est, et usu vertitur in Latinum, significatque pileolum quo Chaldæi utuntur et Persæ. Quandoque autem accipitur pro capitis mitra, juxta illud Exodi : Tiaram pones in capite ejus, scilicet Aaron pontificis. Aliquando vero significat pallium. Et calceamentis et vestibus, missi sunt, id est projecti, in fornacem ignis ardentis. Ideo forsitan jussit eos mitti in ignem indutos, ut diutius torquerentur.
paras.en: [[3:21|And immediately these men|Et confestim viri illi]], the three of them, [[3:21|were bound|vincti]] by the feet, [[3:21|with their coats|cum braccis]] [*braccæ*, breeches]: for which word Aquila and Theodotion said *sarabalia*, which are taken here for coverings of the thighs and shins, according to Jerome and Albert; [[3:21|and their caps|et tiaris]]. *Tiara*, according to Jerome, is Greek, and has passed by use into Latin, and signifies a little cap which the Chaldeans and Persians wear. But sometimes it is taken for a mitre for the head, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 29:6|thou shalt put the mitre upon his head|Tiaram pones in capite ejus]] [the Latin there has *tiara*], that is, the head of Aaron the high priest. And sometimes it signifies a cloak. [[3:21|and their shoes, and their garments|Et calceamentis et vestibus]], [[3:21|were cast|missi sunt]], that is, thrown, [[3:21|into the furnace of burning fire|in fornacem ignis ardentis]]. Perhaps he commanded them to be cast into the fire clothed so that they might be tormented the longer.

paras.t: Nam jussio regis urgebat. Passionati enim, potissime iracundi, cum impetu in optata feruntur, nec pensant quid imminet. Fornax autem succensa erat nimis, videlicet septuplum plus solito. Porro viros illos fortissimos, qui miserant in fornacem Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago, interfecit flamma ignis fornacis. Hoc dicitur hic per anticipationem, quia, ut infra in isto dicetur capitulo, combusti sunt quum angelus descendisset in fornacem, flammamque excussisset. Quod factum est, ut rex non solum de miraculo formidaret, sed et exercitus sui damna sentiret.
paras.en: [[3:22|For the king's commandment was urgent|Nam jussio regis urgebat]]. For those in the grip of passion, the angry above all, are borne headlong towards what they desire, and do not weigh what is impending. [[3:22|and the furnace was heated exceedingly|Fornax autem succensa erat nimis]], namely seven times more than usual. [[3:22|And the flame of the fire slew those men that had cast in Sidrach, Misach, and Abdenago|Porro viros illos fortissimos, qui miserant in fornacem Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago, interfecit flamma ignis fornacis]]. This is said here by anticipation, because, as will be said below in this chapter, they were burnt when the angel had come down into the furnace and driven out the flame[[3:49||]]. This was done so that the king might not only be afraid at the miracle, but also feel the loss to his army.

paras.t: Viri autem hi tres, Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago, ceciderunt projecti in medio camini ignis ardentis, ubi flamma fuit calidior, colligati, id est pedibus vincti, vel et ipsi tres simul ligati, ut pœnas suas mutuo magis sentirent.
paras.en: [[3:23|But these three men, that is, Sidrach, Misach, and Abdenago|Viri autem hi tres, Sidrach, Misach et Abdenago]], [[3:23|fell down|ceciderunt]], being thrown, [[3:23|in the midst of the furnace of burning fire|in medio camini ignis ardentis]], where the flame was hottest, [[3:23|bound|colligati]], that is, bound by the feet, or else the three of them bound together, so that each might feel his pains the more through the others.

paras.t: Quæ sequuntur, in Hebraicis voluminibus non reperi. Hæc verba non sunt de textu, sed Hieronymus ea inseruit, quia ut ait in Prologo hujus Prophetæ, hymnus seu canticum trium puerorum cum verbis statim sequentibus, in Hebræo non continentur. Et sicut in Prologo refert Hieronymus, quidam inter Hebræos præceptor arguebat ista non esse de textu, eo quod verisimile non sit, pueris istis tantum otium in fornace fuisse, ut metro luderent, omnesque creaturas ad Dei invitarent præconium. Verumtamen quidquid sit de veritate seu conclusione, ratio ista non valet : imo valde credibile est, quod quum pueri isti in medio ignis tantam Dei circa se pietatem sentirent, ut non solum non læderentur, sed velut rore refrigerarentur, adversariosque sentirent comburi, et angelum Dei adesse, mirabiliter inflammati sint ad Dei præconium, et omnia ad ejus invitaverint laudem, ita quod erant in otio contemplationis mirabili.
paras.en: *What follows I have not found in the Hebrew volumes.* These words are not of the text, but Jerome inserted them, because, as he says in the Prologue to this Prophet, the hymn or canticle of the three youths, with the words immediately following it, is not contained in the Hebrew. And, as Jerome relates in the Prologue, a certain teacher among the Hebrews argued that these things are not of the text, since it is not likely that these youths had so much leisure in the furnace that they could play at metre and invite all creatures to the praise of God. Yet whatever be the truth of the conclusion, that reason is worthless: nay, it is very credible that when these youths in the midst of the fire felt so great a mercy of God about them that they were not only unharmed but cooled as if by dew, and felt their adversaries being burnt, and the angel of God present, they were wonderfully inflamed to the praise of God and invited all things to praise him, so that they were indeed at leisure, in a wondrous leisure of contemplation [Denis turns the rabbi's *otium*, "leisure", into the *otium contemplationis* of the contemplative life].

paras.t: Et ambulabant in medio flammæ, laudantes Deum et benedicentes Domino : laudantes eum de sua bonitate in se, et benedicentes eidem de effectibus pietatis suæ et æquitatis. Et hoc grande fuit miraculum, quod eorum vincula sunt combusta, ita ut ambularent, corpora autem manserunt illæsa.
paras.en: [[3:24|And they walked in the midst of the flame, praising God, and blessing the Lord|Et ambulabant in medio flammæ, laudantes Deum et benedicentes Domino]]: praising him for his goodness in himself, and blessing him for the effects of his mercy and equity. And this was a great miracle, that their bonds were burnt, so that they walked, but their bodies remained unharmed.

paras.t: Stans autem Azarias, qui inter tres forte senior ac principalior fuit, oravit sic, ut statim subdetur. Aperiensque os suum. Hoc dicitur, ad insinuandum quod sapientissime et cum deliberatione locutus est. In medio ignis, ait. Stetit mente erectus et constans, corpore quoque elevatus ad Deum, suamque orationem laudibus Dei commiscuit, ut exaudibilior esset, juxta illud in Psalmo : Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero.
paras.en: [[3:25|Then Azarias standing up|Stans autem Azarias]], who was perhaps the eldest and chief among the three, [[3:25|prayed in this manner|oravit sic]], as is set down immediately after. [[3:25|and opening his mouth|Aperiensque os suum]]. This is said to suggest that he spoke most wisely and with deliberation. [[3:25|in the midst of the fire, he said|In medio ignis, ait]]. He stood upright and constant in mind, raised up to God in body too, and he mingled his prayer with the praises of God, that it might be the more readily heard, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 17:4|Praising, I will call upon the Lord: and I shall be saved from my enemies|Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero]].

paras.t: Benedictus es, Domine Deus patrum nostrorum Abrahæ, Isaac et Jacob : qui licet sis omnium Deus ac Dominus per creationem, illorum tamen specialiter Deus ac Dominus es per prædestinationem, miserationem, providentiamque et gratiam valde specialem. Unde quum in Exodo Moyses nomen Dei a Deo sciscitaretur, responsum est ei a Deo : Hæc dices filiis Israel : Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob, misit me ad vos : hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc memoriale meum in generationem et generationem. Dicitur autem Deus benedictus, tanquam fons omnis benedictionis, et omni bono dicto dicendus seu appellandus, utpote omni præclara nominatione prædignus, cui omne bonum est adscribendum. Et laudabilis, tanquam virtuosus et bonus simpliciter ac perfecte. Laus enim virtuti ac bonitati impenditur ac debetur. Et gloriosum nomen tuum nominatum, scilicet tu ipse, in sæcula : gloriosum, inquam, id est omni fama et laude dignissimum seu vulgatum, vel cum laude cognitum, secundum quod gloria dicitur clara cum laude notitia ; gloriosum quoque, id est felicitate, jucunditate et excellentia plenum.
paras.en: [[3:26|Blessed art thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers|Benedictus es, Domine Deus patrum nostrorum]], Abraham, Isaac and Jacob [these names, printed as part of the text, are not in the Clementine Vulgate]: who, although thou art the God and Lord of all by creation, art yet in a special way their God and Lord by predestination, mercy, providence and a very special grace. Hence when in Exodus Moses asked God for God's name, it was answered him by God: [[Ex 3:15|Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: The Lord God of your fathers the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob hath sent me to you; this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations|Hæc dices filiis Israel : Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob, misit me ad vos : hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc memoriale meum in generationem et generationem]]. Now God is called *blessed* as the fount of all blessing, and as one to be spoken of or called by every good word [*benedictus*, literally "well spoken of"], being worthy of every illustrious name, he to whom every good thing is to be ascribed. [[3:26|worthy of praise|Et laudabilis]] [Denis reads *laudabilis* and refers it to God; the Clementine text has *laudabile*, of the name], as being virtuous and good simply and perfectly. For praise is paid and owed to virtue and goodness. [[3:26|and glorious|Et gloriosum]] [[3:26|thy name|nomen tuum]] named, that is, thou thyself, [[3:26|for ever|in sæcula]]: glorious, I say, that is, most worthy of all fame and praise, or spread abroad, or known with praise, according as glory is called clear knowledge joined with praise; glorious too, that is, full of happiness, joy and excellence.

paras.t: Quoniam justus es in omnibus quæ fecisti nobis, id est in persecutionibus et flagellis nobis a te inflictis, qui das unicuique quod meretur. Sic et Psalmista decantat : Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum ; itemque, Quoniam justus Dominus et justitias dilexit, æquitatem vidit vultus ejus. Et universa opera tua vera, veritate naturæ seu entis, in quantum conformia sunt rationibus idealibus quas habent in mente divina. Vera sunt quoque veritate justitiæ, in quantum primæ et increatæ rectitudini ac sapientiæ consona. Et viæ tuæ rectæ, id est, processus tui in rerum dispositione sunt ordinati. Viæ quoque Dei, sunt præcepta et consilia ejus : de quibus in Proverbiis legitur, Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ. Rursus, viæ Dei dicuntur ejus vestigia.
paras.en: [[3:27|For thou art just in all that thou hast done to us|Quoniam justus es in omnibus quæ fecisti nobis]], that is, in the persecutions and scourges inflicted on us by thee, who givest to each what he deserves. So too the Psalmist sings: [[Ps 118:137|Thou art just, O Lord: and thy judgment is right|Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum]]; and again: [[Ps 10:8|For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: his countenance hath beheld righteousness|Quoniam justus Dominus et justitias dilexit, æquitatem vidit vultus ejus]]. [[3:27|and all thy works are true|Et universa opera tua vera]], with the truth of nature or of being, inasmuch as they conform to the ideal reasons [that is, the patterns of all things in the mind of God] which they have in the divine mind. They are true also with the truth of justice, inasmuch as they accord with the first and uncreated rectitude and wisdom. [[3:27|and thy ways right|Et viæ tuæ rectæ]], that is, thy proceedings in the ordering of things are well ordered. The ways of God are also his precepts and counsels, of which we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:17|Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable|Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ ejus pacificæ]]. Again, the ways of God are said to be his footsteps.

paras.t: Et omnia judicia tua vera, id est justa ac sapientialia. Judicia autem Dei dicuntur dupliciter : Primo, secundum quod sunt in ipso Deo omnia judicante : in quo non sunt plura, nisi per relationem ad judicata, quemadmodum ideæ multæ dicuntur per respectum ad ideata. Hæc vero judicia quid sunt, nisi censuræ sapientiæ Dei, qua de omnibus rectissime judicat ? De quibus ait Apostolus : Quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus ! Secundo, dicuntur Dei judicia effectus divinæ justitiæ, scilicet retributiones aut dispositiones in rebus. De quibus ait Psalmista : Judicia Domini vera, justificata in semetipsa. Denique ponitur judicium discretionis, quo Deus in præsenti inter electos reprobosque discernit, illos misericorditer convertendo, istos juste deserendo, de quo loquitur Christus, Nunc judicium est mundi : et istud occultum est. Aliud judicium est remunerationis, quod in fine sæculi, quantum ad omnes, apertissime fiet, juxta illud Psalmi : Judicabit orbem terrarum in justitia, et populos in æquitate. Porro, secundum Albertum, per judicia intelliguntur hoc loco punitiones a Deo inflictæ. Sic namque exponit : Judicia tua vera, quæ scilicet contra nos fecisti. Huic Dei præconio consonat illud Apocalypsis : Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens ; justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum ; Domine Deus omnipotens, justa et vera judicia tua.
paras.en: [[3:27|and all thy judgments true|Et omnia judicia tua vera]], that is, just and wise. Now the judgments of God are spoken of in two ways. First, as they are in God himself, who judges all things: in him they are not many except by relation to the things judged, as the ideas are called many with respect to the things patterned on them. And what are these judgments but the decrees of the wisdom of God, by which he judges most rightly of all things? Of these the Apostle says: [[Rom 11:33|How incomprehensible are his judgments|Quam incomprehensibilia sunt judicia ejus]]! Secondly, the effects of the divine justice, that is, retributions or dispositions in things, are called the judgments of God. Of these the Psalmist says: [[Ps 18:10|the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves|Judicia Domini vera, justificata in semetipsa]]. Further, there is the judgment of discernment, by which God in the present life discerns between the elect and the reprobate, converting the former in mercy and justly forsaking the latter; of which Christ speaks: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]; and this judgment is hidden. The other is the judgment of reward, which at the end of the world will be made most openly as regards all men, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 97:9|He shall judge the world with justice, and the people with equity|Judicabit orbem terrarum in justitia, et populos in æquitate]]. Moreover, according to Albert, by *judgments* are understood here the punishments inflicted by God. For he expounds it thus: [[3:27|thy judgments true|Judicia tua vera]], namely those which thou hast executed against us. With this praise of God agrees that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 15:3|Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty. Just and true are thy ways, O King of ages|Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua, Domine Deus omnipotens ; justæ et veræ sunt viæ tuæ, Rex sæculorum]]; [[Apoc 16:7|O Lord God Almighty, true and just are thy judgments|Domine Deus omnipotens, justa et vera judicia tua]].

paras.t: Judicia enim vera veritate justitiæ fecisti, id est, supplicia nostris demeritis debita inflixisti, juxta omnia, id est in omnibus, vel secundum universa afflictiva, quæ induxisti super nos per Chaldæos, et super civitatem sanctam patrum nostrorum Jerusalem. Quæ dicitur sancta, quia divino cultui fuit specialiter deputata, et divinis sacramentis atque obsequiis sanctificata : in qua multi Vatum ac Patriarcharum Domino servierunt in sanctitate atque justitia; de qua in Isaia legitur : Civitas sancta tua, facta est deserta. Quæ postea per Christi in ea præsentationem, personalem præsentiam, visitationem, prædicationem, miraculosam operationem, novissimam Cœnam, Eucharistiæ institutionem, passionem, Spiritus Sancti missionem, Apostolorum doctrinam, primitivæ Ecclesiæ sacratissimam conversationem, multorumque martyrum occisionem, excellentius sanctificata dignoscitur. Propter quod Matthæus dicit : Multa sanctorum corpora surrexerunt, et venerunt in sanctam civitatem, et apparuerunt multis.
paras.en: [[3:28|For thou hast executed true judgments|Judicia enim vera]] with the truth of justice, that is, thou hast inflicted the punishments due to our demerits, [[3:28|in all the things|juxta omnia]], that is, in all things, or according to all the afflictions, [[3:28|that thou hast brought upon us|quæ induxisti super nos]] by the Chaldeans, [[3:28|and upon Jerusalem, the holy city of our fathers|et super civitatem sanctam patrum nostrorum Jerusalem]]. It is called holy because it was specially set apart for the worship of God and sanctified by divine sacraments and services: in it many of the Prophets and Patriarchs served the Lord in holiness and justice; of it we read in Isaias: [[Is 64:10|The city of thy sanctuary is become a desert|Civitas sancta tua, facta est deserta]] [Denis reads *Civitas sancta tua*, "thy holy city"]. Afterwards it is known to have been more excellently sanctified through Christ's presentation in it, his personal presence, visitation, preaching, miraculous working, the Last Supper, the institution of the Eucharist, the passion, the sending of the Holy Ghost, the teaching of the Apostles, the most holy way of life of the primitive Church, and the slaying of many martyrs. Wherefore Matthew says: [[Matt 27:52|many bodies of the saints that had slept arose|Multa sanctorum corpora surrexerunt]], [[Matt 27:53|came into the holy city and appeared to many|et venerunt in sanctam civitatem, et apparuerunt multis]].

paras.t: Quia in veritate justitiæ, quæ est vera justitia; in vera quoque verborum tuorum propheticorum impletione atque veraciter; et judicio justo, quod a veritate et æquitate procedit; induxisti omnia hæc afflictoria super nos per Chaldæos, propter peccata nostra, qui nullum malum relinquis inultum, secundum illud Job, Deus inultum abire non patitur.
paras.en: [[3:28|for according to truth|Quia in veritate]] of justice, which is true justice, and also in the true fulfilment of thy prophetic words, and truthfully; [[3:28|and judgment|et judicio]], a just judgment, which proceeds from truth and equity, [[3:28|thou hast brought all these things upon us|induxisti omnia hæc afflictoria super nos]] by the Chaldeans, [[3:28|for our sins|propter peccata nostra]], thou who leavest no evil unpunished, according to that of Job: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]].

paras.t: Quocirca ait Hieronymus : Quando diversis premimur angustiis, ex toto cordis affectu præfata verba loquamur. Et quidquid nobis acciderit, juste nos sustinere fateamur, ut compleatur in nobis quod scriptum est : Exsultaverunt filiæ Judæ propter judicia tua, Domine. Unde et Judith salubriter admonet : Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur ; sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus.
paras.en: Wherefore Jerome says: When we are pressed by various straits, let us speak the aforesaid words with the whole affection of the heart. And whatever befalls us, let us confess that we suffer it justly, that there may be fulfilled in us what is written: [[Ps 96:8|And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, because of thy judgments, O Lord|Exsultaverunt filiæ Judæ propter judicia tua, Domine]]. Hence Judith too gives this wholesome warning: [[Jdt 8:26|As for us therefore let us not revenge ourselves for these things which we suffer|Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur]]; [[Jdt 8:27|But esteeming these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve, let us believe that these scourges of the Lord, with which like servants we are chastised, have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction|sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse, flagella Domini, quasi servi qui corripimur, ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus]].

paras.t: Peccavimus enim, et inique egimus, recedentes a te, per mentis aversionem a te summo et incommutabili infinitoque bono, non per corporis motionem directe, scilicet ut est motio corporalis, distantiamque localem, quum vere essentialiterque ubique sis; et deliquimus in omnibus per peccata omissionis : juxta illud Osee, Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo.
paras.en: [[3:29|For we have sinned, and committed iniquity, departing from thee|Peccavimus enim, et inique egimus, recedentes a te]], by the turning away of the mind from thee, the highest, unchangeable and infinite good, not directly by a movement of the body, that is, as bodily motion and distance in place, since thou art truly and essentially everywhere; [[3:29|and we have trespassed in all things|et deliquimus in omnibus]] by sins of omission, according to that of Osee: [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing|Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo]].

paras.t: Et præcepta tua non audivimus interiori auditu per obedientiam et complacentiam; et quidam ita rebelles fuerunt, quod nec corporalibus auribus verba Dei voluerunt audire. Tales quoque fuerunt Judæi tempore Christi, quibus ait : Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit : propterea vos non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis. Denique interiori aure audire, est diligenter advertere, et verbis Dei complacentiam efficientiamque adhibere. Nec observavimus in memoria. Memorialiter autem verborum observatio valet ad repellendum tentationes ac vitia : propter quod ait Psalmista, In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Itaque, dum aliquid cogitamus, affectamus, effamur aut operamur, pensemus an verbis Dei repugnet : quod si ita est, mox ab illo cessemus.
paras.en: [[3:30|And we have not hearkened to thy commandments|Et præcepta tua non audivimus]] with the inward hearing, by obedience and willing assent; and some were so rebellious that they would not hear the words of God even with their bodily ears. Such too were the Jews in the time of Christ, to whom he says: [[John 8:47|He that is of God heareth the words of God. Therefore you hear them not, because you are not of God|Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit : propterea vos non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis]]. Further, to hear with the inward ear is to attend diligently, and to bring to the words of God willing assent and the doing of them. [[3:30|nor have we observed|Nec observavimus]] them in memory. Now the keeping of the words in memory avails to repel temptations and vices; wherefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. And so, whenever we think, desire, speak or do anything, let us weigh whether it is contrary to the words of God; and if it is, let us straightway cease from it.

paras.t: Nec fecimus in opere exteriori sicut præceperas nobis, id est, eo modo ac tali fine non implevimus tua mandata, quo modo et cur ea fieri imperasti. Multi quippe videntur divinis præceptis obtemperare, quantum ad substantiam facti seu operis, non tamen vere obediunt, quia non ad Dei gloriam ex caritate talia agunt. Ut bene nobis esset, præsertim in spiritualibus bonis, ut scilicet bonis gratiæ in præsenti, et bonis gloriæ in futuro ditaremur. Ex quo innotescit, quod ad nostram utilitatem ac felicitatem, non ad suum profectum aut commodum, Deus jussit nos sibi parere : ipse enim nostrorum bonorum non eget. Omnia tamen ultimate finaliterque refert ad se ipsum, suamque gloriam : sed et nostram ipse salutem, quantum in se est, se desiderare seu velle insinuat; et filiis Israel etiam temporalium abundantiam, si sibi efficaciter deservirent, spopondit. Hinc in Deuteronomio habetur : Dixit Dominus ad Moysen : Quis det talem eos mentem habere, ut timeant me, et custodiant universa mandata mea, et bene sit eis et filiis eorum post eos in sempiternum? Præterea, secundum Albertum, duo peccata sunt, nolle audire, et auditui nolle obedire. Contra quod fertur in Psalmo : Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra.
paras.en: [[3:30|nor done|Nec fecimus]] in outward work [[3:30|as thou hadst commanded us|sicut præceperas nobis]], that is, we have not fulfilled thy commandments in the manner and for the end in which and for which thou didst command them to be done. For many seem to obey the divine precepts as to the substance of the deed or work, yet do not truly obey, because they do not do such things for the glory of God out of charity. [[3:30|that it might go well with us|Ut bene nobis esset]], especially in spiritual goods, namely that we might be enriched with the goods of grace in the present and the goods of glory in the future. From this it is made known that God commanded us to obey him for our own profit and happiness, not for his own advancement or advantage: for he has no need of our goods[[Ps 15:2||]]. Yet he refers all things ultimately and finally to himself and his own glory; but he also gives us to understand that he himself, as far as in him lies, desires or wills our salvation; and to the children of Israel he promised even an abundance of temporal goods if they served him faithfully. Hence we have in Deuteronomy: The Lord said to Moses: [[Deut 5:29|Who shall give them to have such a mind, to fear me, and to keep all my commandments at all times, that it may be well with them and with their children for ever?|Quis det talem eos mentem habere, ut timeant me, et custodiant universa mandata mea, et bene sit eis et filiis eorum post eos in sempiternum?]] Moreover, according to Albert, there are two sins: to be unwilling to hear, and to be unwilling to obey what is heard. Against which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 94:8|To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts|Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra]].

paras.t: Insuper advertendum, quod præinducta verba humillimæ confessionis tres pueri isti non in sua, sed in sui populi persona effati sunt, quia et ipsi pars erant Israeliticæ plebis. Ipsi namque innocentes fuerunt, præsertim ab eis sceleribus propter quæ tradita fuit Judæa Chaldæis. Juxta quem modum etiam Esdras oravit : Deus meus, confundor levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum. Hinc ait Hieronymus : Certe tres pueri nec peccaverant, nec ejus ætatis erant, quando ducti sunt in captivitatem, ut propter sua vitia punirentur : ergo quomodo hi ex persona populi loquuntur, sic illud Apostoli legendum est : Non enim quod volo, hoc ago; sed quod nolo, hoc operor; et cetera quæ in eodem scripta sunt loco.
paras.en: Furthermore it is to be noted that these three youths uttered the foregoing words of most humble confession not in their own person but in the person of their people, since they too were part of the Israelite people. For they themselves were innocent, especially of those crimes for which Judea was delivered to the Chaldeans. In the same way Esdras too prayed: [[1 Esd 9:6|My God I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face to thee: for our iniquities are multiplied over our heads, and our sins are grown up even unto heaven|Deus meus, confundor levare faciem meam ad te, quoniam iniquitates nostræ multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, et peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum]]. Hence Jerome says: Certainly the three youths had not sinned, nor were they of such an age, when they were led into captivity, as to be punished for their own vices: therefore, just as these speak in the person of the people, so must that saying of the Apostle be read: [[Rom 7:15|For I do not that good which I will|Non enim quod volo, hoc ago]]; [[Rom 7:15|but the evil which I hate, that I do|sed quod nolo, hoc operor]]; and the rest that is written in the same place.

paras.t: Omnia ergo quæ induxisti super nos, et universa quæ fecisti nobis, in vero, id est justo, judicio fecisti.
paras.en: [[3:31|Wherefore, all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us|Omnia ergo quæ induxisti super nos, et universa quæ fecisti nobis]], [[3:31|thou hast done in true|in vero]], that is, just, [[3:31|judgment|judicio fecisti]].

paras.t: Et tradidisti nos in manibus inimicorum iniquorum et pessimorum, videlicet Chaldæorum : quia in quantum inimici, voluerunt nocere; quia iniqui, nulla virtutis honestate reprimebantur; et pessimi erant, quia quo ceteris gentibus potentiores, eo et crudeliores ac superbiores, et idolis servientes ; prævaricatorumque, id est transgressorum etiam legis naturalis, naturalisque pietatis : de cujus dictamine est, ut quod vis fieri tibi, facias alteri, et quod non vis tibi fieri, non facias alii. Unde in Evangelio loquitur Christus : Quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, hæc facite illis. Et Tobias : Quod ab alio oderis fieri tibi, vide ne aliquando aliis facias. Quod tamen de rationabili velle nolleque dicitur. Et regi Nabuchodonosor, injusto contra proximos quos oppressit, et pessimo contra Deum, cujus sibi usurpavit honorem, idola colens et se in statua adorari præcipiens, ultra omnem terram, id est præ cunctis habitatoribus terræ : nam crudelissimus fuit, et innumerabiles gentes undique devastavit. Nec obstat quod in Jeremia et Ezechiele Deus eum nominavit servum suum. Sic nempe eum appellat, quoniam divinæ fuit justitiæ instrumentum in punitione malorum : quod tamen intentione fecit perversa; postea vero pœnituit, ut infra describitur.
paras.en: [[3:32|And thou hast delivered us into the hands of our enemies|Et tradidisti nos in manibus inimicorum]] [[3:32|that are unjust|iniquorum]], [[3:32|and most wicked|et pessimorum]], namely of the Chaldeans: enemies, because as enemies they wished to do harm; unjust, because they were restrained by no honesty of virtue; and they were most wicked, because the mightier they were than other nations, the crueller and prouder they were, and they served idols; [[3:32|and prevaricators|prævaricatorumque]], that is, transgressors even of the natural law and of natural piety, whose dictate is that what thou wouldst have done to thee thou shouldst do to another, and what thou wouldst not have done to thee thou shouldst not do to another. Hence Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:12|whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them|Quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, hæc facite illis]]. And Tobias: [[Tob 4:16|See thou never do to another what thou wouldst hate to have done to thee by another|Quod ab alio oderis fieri tibi, vide ne aliquando aliis facias]]. This, however, is said of rational willing and not willing. [[3:32|and to a king|Et regi]] Nabuchodonosor, [[3:32|unjust|injusto]] towards the neighbours whom he oppressed, [[3:32|and most wicked|et pessimo]] towards God, whose honour he usurped for himself, worshipping idols and commanding himself to be adored in the statue, [[3:32|beyond all that are upon the earth|ultra omnem terram]], that is, above all the inhabitants of the earth: for he was most cruel, and laid waste innumerable nations on every side. Nor does it stand in the way that in Jeremias and Ezechiel God named him his servant[[Jer 25:9||]][[Ezech 29:20||]]. For he calls him so because he was the instrument of divine justice in the punishment of the wicked, which, however, he did with a perverse intention; but afterwards he repented, as is described below.

paras.t: Verumtamen circa hæc quæstio oritur, quomodo Deus justus justo judicio cum injustis Judæis etiam justos Judæos manibus tradidit Chaldæorum. Nam et Ezechiel ad terram Israel ait : Ecce ego ad te, et ejiciam gladium meum de vagina sua, et occidam in te justum et impium. Et respondendum, quod Deus sublimis et benedictus, justus et sapiens, quandoque etiam justos impiis tradit torquendos absque eorum demerito seu peccatis : et hoc, justo judicio, ut patet in Job. Non enim pro sola culpa infligitur pœna a Deo, sed et ob alias causas multiplices, scilicet ad virtutis exercitationem, ad justitiæ justorum ostensionem, ad aliorum ædificationem, ad bonorum profectum et gloriam ampliorem, ad divinæ potestatis declarationem, prout Spiritu Sancto præstante, opere isto completo, super Job plenius declarabo.
paras.en: Yet about these words a question arises: how did the just God, by a just judgment, deliver into the hands of the Chaldeans the just Jews too, along with the unjust? For Ezechiel also says to the land of Israel: [[Ezech 21:3|Behold I come against thee, and I will draw forth my sword out of its sheath, and will cut off in thee the just, and the wicked|Ecce ego ad te, et ejiciam gladium meum de vagina sua, et occidam in te justum et impium]]. And the answer must be that God, sublime and blessed, just and wise, sometimes delivers even the just to the wicked to be tormented, without any demerit or sins of theirs; and this by a just judgment, as is plain in Job. For punishment is inflicted by God not for guilt alone, but also for many other causes: namely, for the exercise of virtue, for the showing forth of the justice of the just, for the edification of others, for the advancement and greater glory of the good, for the declaration of the divine power; as, by the gift of the Holy Ghost, I shall explain more fully on Job when this work is finished.

paras.t: Et nunc non possumus aperire os, id est, nec adversariis nostris respondere seu resistere possumus, neque nos coram te excusare; et præ confusione vix loqui valemus. Sic et sanctus Job ait : Quia leviter locutus sum, respondere quid possum ? Manum meam ponam super os meum. Et Ezechias in Isaiæ libro : Quid dicam, aut quid respondebo quum ipse fecerim? Confusio et opprobrium, id est materia confusionis interioris, scilicet cordis in conscientia, et exprobrationis exterius, facti sumus servis tuis, et, pro id est, his qui colunt te, quia ad exprobrandum objicimur eis. Unde Glossa ait : Bonis infertur opprobrium et confusio propter nos. Etenim dum justi premuntur ab impiis, malitiosi insultant ceteris justis quasi inaniter colant Deum, qui eos in adversitatibus non tuetur : sicque miseria seu afflictio virtuosi pro opprobrio infertur colentibus Deum ab impiis. Propter quod in Job legitur : Deridetur justi simplicitas. Et in Proverbiis Salomon ait : Abominantur impii justum; et, Viri sanguinum oderunt simplicem; et item, Qui derelinquunt legem, laudant impium. Hinc et Christus orat in Psalmo : Non erubescant in me qui exspectant te, Domine; non confundantur super me qui quærunt te, Deus Israel. De hujusmodi enim eventu dolent viri virtutum, non in quantum habent rationem pœnæ seu adversitatis quantum ad eos; hanc namque per patientiam etiam cum gaudio ferunt : sed ut est culpa gravissima, et velut blasphemia Dei, quoniam derogat providentiæ ejus; et item, ut est scandalizativum pusillorum, nocivum quoque perversis ita agentibus.
paras.en: [[3:33|And now we cannot open our mouths|Et nunc non possumus aperire os]]: that is, we can neither answer nor resist our adversaries, nor excuse ourselves before thee; and for confusion we are scarcely able to speak. So too holy Job says: [[Job 39:34|What can I answer, who hath spoken inconsiderately? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.|Quia leviter locutus sum, respondere quid possum ? Manum meam ponam super os meum]] And Ezechias in the book of Isaias: [[Is 38:15|What shall I say|Quid dicam]], or what shall I answer, since I myself have done it? [Denis's reading; the Vulgate has "or what shall he answer for me, whereas he himself hath done it"] [[3:33|a shame, and a reproach|Confusio et opprobrium]], that is, matter for confusion within, namely of the heart in the conscience, and for reproach without, [[3:33|we are become|facti sumus]] [[3:33|to thy servants, and|servis tuis, et]] (*and* standing for *that is*) [[3:33|to them that worship thee|his qui colunt te]]: because we are held up to them for reproach. Hence the Gloss says: Reproach and confusion are brought upon the good on our account. For while the just are oppressed by the wicked, the malicious mock the other just men, as though they worshipped God in vain, since he does not protect them in adversity; and so the misery or affliction of the virtuous man is brought by the wicked as a reproach upon those who worship God. For this reason we read in Job: [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur justi simplicitas]]. And in Proverbs Solomon says: [[Prov 29:27|the wicked loathe them that are in the right way|Abominantur impii justum]] [Denis has "the just man" for "them that are in the right way"]; and, [[Prov 29:10|Bloodthirsty men hate the upright|Viri sanguinum oderunt simplicem]]; and again, [[Prov 28:4|They that forsake the law, praise the wicked man|Qui derelinquunt legem, laudant impium]]. Hence Christ too prays in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:7|Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord|Non erubescant in me qui exspectant te, Domine]]; [[Ps 68:7|Let them not be confounded on my account, who seek thee, O God of Israel|non confundantur super me qui quærunt te, Deus Israel]]. For men of virtue grieve at an event of this kind, not in so far as it has the character of punishment or adversity as regards themselves, for this they bear with patience, even with joy; but inasmuch as it is a most grievous fault, and as it were a blasphemy against God, since it detracts from his providence; and again, inasmuch as it gives scandal to the little ones, and is harmful too to the perverse who act so.

paras.t: Ne, quæsumus, etc. Secundum Albertum, post et juxta confessionem ponit orationem sequentem : quæ ex quinque conficitur, scilicet gloria nominis Dei, suffragio paternæ intercessionis, confessione humiliationis, sacrificio contribulati cordis, sequela perseverantissimæ voluntatis. Hæc quinque consideranti sequentia innotescent. Quantum ad primum, orditur loquens in sua et sociorum suorum persona :
paras.en: [[3:34|we beseech thee|Ne, quæsumus]], etc. According to Albert, after the confession and in keeping with it he sets down the prayer that follows, which is made up of five things: namely, the glory of God's name, the support of the fathers' intercession, the confession of humiliation, the sacrifice of a contrite heart, and the following of a most persevering will. These five will become clear to one who considers what follows. As to the first, he begins, speaking in his own person and in that of his companions:

paras.t: Ne, quæsumus, tradas nos hostibus in perpetuum affligendos. Quasi dicat : Non ultra vires permittas nos tribulari, nec pœna hæc captivitatis nimium protrahatur, quamvis ad tempus duret. Hoc oravit, ut cultus Dei in Jerusalem reformaretur, et ne plebs Israelitica adhuc imperfecta, adversitatibus victa, ad impatientiam verteretur, atque a Dei cultu ad idololatriam declinaret. Denique virtuosi tribulationibus cincti, ad requiem beatitudinemque licenter adspirant : sicut et David in Psalmo et verbis libri Regum, a Saule frequenter eripi flagitavit. Unde et in Isaia habetur : Ne irascaris, Domine, satis. Hinc in fine Threnorum orans Dominum Jeremias : Quare, inquit, in perpetuum oblivisceris nostri, derelinques nos in longitudinem dierum? Propter nomen tuum, id est, propter tui ipsius bonitatem et pietatem nos audi, etsi non propter merita nostra : sicut et Psalmista precatur, Propter nomen tuum, Domine, propitiaberis peccato meo; et denuo, Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu, propter bonitatem tuam, Domine. Vel, Propter nomen tuum, id est ob tui ipsius honorem et gloriam, ut in nostra liberatione tu glorificeris, lauderis, omniumque tuorum liberator ab omnibus agnoscaris. Ad utrumque autem sensum pertinet illud Ezechielis : Non propter vos ego faciam, ait Dominus Deus, sed propter nomen sanctum meum.
paras.en: [[3:34|We beseech thee|Ne, quæsumus]], [[3:34|deliver us not up|tradas nos]] to our enemies to be afflicted [[3:34|for ever|in perpetuum]] [Denis's text adds "to our enemies … to be afflicted"]. As if to say: Do not let us be troubled beyond our strength, nor let this punishment of captivity be drawn out too long, though it last for a time. He prayed this so that the worship of God might be restored in Jerusalem, and lest the Israelite people, still imperfect, overcome by adversities, should turn to impatience and fall away from the worship of God to idolatry. Moreover the virtuous, when hemmed in by tribulations, may lawfully aspire to rest and blessedness: as David too, in the Psalms and in the words of the books of Kings, often begged to be rescued from Saul. Hence in Isaias too we have: [[Is 64:9|Be not very angry, O Lord|Ne irascaris, Domine, satis]]. Hence at the end of the Lamentations Jeremias, praying to the Lord, says: [[Lam 5:20|Why|Quare]], he says, [[Lam 5:20|wilt thou forget us for ever? why wilt thou forsake us for a long time?|in perpetuum oblivisceris nostri, derelinques nos in longitudinem dierum?]] [[3:34|For thy name's sake|Propter nomen tuum]]: that is, hear us for the sake of thine own goodness and loving-kindness, even if not for our merits; as the Psalmist too prays, [[Ps 24:11|For thy name's sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin|Propter nomen tuum, Domine, propitiaberis peccato meo]]; and again, [[Ps 24:7|According to thy mercy remember thou me: for thy goodness' sake, O Lord|Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu, propter bonitatem tuam, Domine]]. Or, [[3:34|For thy name's sake|Propter nomen tuum]], that is, for thine own honour and glory, so that in our deliverance thou mayest be glorified and praised, and acknowledged by all as the deliverer of all thine own. And to both senses belongs that word of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:22|It is not for your sake that I will do this|Non propter vos ego faciam]], says the Lord God, [[Ezech 36:22|but for my holy name's sake|sed propter nomen sanctum meum]].

paras.t: Et ne dissipes, id est, destrui seu auferri permittas, testamentum tuum, id est legem per Moysen datam : quæ dissipatur dum ejus cultores tolluntur. Sic sumitur testamentum ad Hebræos octavo, quo verba Jeremiæ allegantur, et inter cetera dicitur : Quoniam ipsi non permanserunt in testamento meo, ego neglexi eos, dicit Dominus. Vel, Ne dissipes testamentum tuum, id est, fœdus seu pactum quod cum nostris patribus percussisti in datione legis, quod scilicet ipsis eorumque posteris propitius esses, atque in tribulatione ad te vociferantes exaudires : juxta illud Nehemiæ : Memento verbi quod mandasti Moysi servo tuo, dicens : Quum transgressi fueritis, ego disperdam vos in populos; et si revertamini ad me, ut custodiatis præcepta mea, etiam si abducti fueritis ad extrema cœli, inde congregabo vos. Neque auferas misericordiam tuam, id est pietatis tuæ effectum, a nobis : scilicet, pacem pectoris, pacemque temporis, quibus ad pacem æternitatis ducamur, da nobis. Albertus prædictum locum ita exponit : Ne dissipes testamentum tuum, quo testatus es te nobis daturum ; secundum illud : Memorari testamenti sui sancti ; jusjurandum quod juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum, daturum se nobis. Neque auferas misericordiam, qua te promisisti nasciturum ex nobis.
paras.en: [[3:34|and abolish not|Et ne dissipes]], that is, do not allow to be destroyed or taken away, [[3:34|thy covenant|testamentum tuum]], that is, the law given through Moses, which is abolished when its worshippers are taken away. *Testament* [*testamentum*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "covenant" in this verse] is taken in this sense in the eighth chapter to the Hebrews, where the words of Jeremias are brought forward and it is said among other things: [[Heb 8:9|because they continued not in my testament: and I regarded them not, saith the Lord|Quoniam ipsi non permanserunt in testamento meo, ego neglexi eos, dicit Dominus]]. Or, [[3:34|abolish not thy covenant|Ne dissipes testamentum tuum]], that is, the treaty or pact which thou didst strike with our fathers in the giving of the law: namely, that thou wouldst be gracious to them and to their posterity, and wouldst hear them when they cried to thee in tribulation; according to that word of Nehemias: [[2 Esd 1:8|Remember the word that thou commandedst to Moses thy servant, saying: If you shall transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations|Memento verbi quod mandasti Moysi servo tuo, dicens : Quum transgressi fueritis, ego disperdam vos in populos]]; [[2 Esd 1:9|But if you return to me, and keep my commandments|et si revertamini ad me, ut custodiatis præcepta mea]], [[2 Esd 1:9|though you should be led away to the uttermost parts of the world, I will gather you from thence|etiam si abducti fueritis ad extrema cœli, inde congregabo vos]]. [[3:35|And take not away thy mercy|Neque auferas misericordiam tuam]], that is, the effect of thy loving-kindness, [[3:35|from us|a nobis]]: that is, give us peace of heart and peace in our times, by which we may be led to the peace of eternity. Albert expounds the passage above thus: *Abolish not thy covenant*, by which thou didst testify that thou wouldst give thyself to us; according to that word: [[Luke 1:72|to remember his holy testament|Memorari testamenti sui sancti]]: [[Luke 1:73|The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant to us|jusjurandum quod juravit ad Abraham patrem nostrum, daturum se nobis]]. *And take not away thy mercy*, by which thou didst promise that thou wouldst be born of us.

paras.t: Propter Abraham dilectum tuum, id est valde dilectum et ex pluribus præelectum, cui et multa dilectionis indicia ostendisti : ut patet in Genesi. Quidam dicunt Abraham dilectum Dei vocari, quoniam primus fuit electus a Deo ex idololatris, et quia primo factæ sunt ei promissiones apertæ de Christo : quæ si ita se habeant, in fine articuli hujus clarebit. Et Isaac servum tuum, servitute filialis timoris, cui dicitur, Euge, serve bone, intra in gaudium Domini tui ; non servitute timoris servilis, cui dicitur in Joanne, Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in æternum. Ideo autem specialiter servus vocatur, secundum Albertum et alios, quia simpliciter obedivit, quando pater ejus voluit eum Deo offerre. Tunc enim ad virilem pervenit ætatem, et tamen a patre sene se permisit ligari, et ad immolationem accessit spontanee, ut Josephus primo Antiquitatum libro describit, imo ex Genesi comprobatur. Et Israel, id est Jacob patriarcham, sanctum tuum, id est sanctificatum a te : qui et eximiæ exstitit sanctitatis, sicut in Genesi patet ; videturque Augustinus sentire, quod sanctificatus fuerit in utero matris, quia adhuc exsistentem in utero Deus dilexit. Primo quoque sancto Jacob in somno ostensa est sanctitas templi ac cultus divini, secundum Albertum, ut in Genesi inducitur : ubi et legitur, quod speciali cultu vovit se colere Deum, Erit (inquiens) mihi Dominus in Deum. Illud autem sanctum vocatur, quod divino cultui applicatur.
paras.en: [[3:35|for the sake of Abraham, thy beloved|Propter Abraham dilectum tuum]], that is, greatly beloved and chosen out of many, to whom thou didst also show many tokens of love, as is plain in Genesis. Some say that Abraham is called the beloved of God because he was the first to be chosen by God from among idolaters, and because the open promises concerning Christ were first made to him: whether this is so will become clear at the end of this article. [[3:35|and Isaac, thy servant|Et Isaac servum tuum]], by the service of filial fear, to which it is said, [[Matt 25:21|Well done, good and faithful servant|Euge, serve bone]], [[Matt 25:21|enter thou into the joy of thy lord|intra in gaudium Domini tui]][[Matt 25:23||]]; not by the service of servile fear, to which it is said in John, [[John 8:35|Now the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the son abideth for ever.|Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in æternum]] He is called servant in a special way, according to Albert and others, because he obeyed simply when his father wished to offer him to God. For at that time he had come to man's estate, and yet he let himself be bound by his aged father, and went of his own accord to be sacrificed, as Josephus describes in the first book of the Antiquities; indeed it is proved from Genesis[[Gen 22:9||]]. [[3:35|and Israel|Et Israel]], that is, the patriarch Jacob, [[3:35|thy holy one|sanctum tuum]], that is, sanctified by thee: who was also of outstanding holiness, as is plain in Genesis; and Augustine seems to hold that he was sanctified in his mother's womb, since God loved him while he was still in the womb. To holy Jacob also, according to Albert, the holiness of the temple and of divine worship was first shown, in sleep, as is related in Genesis[[Gen 28:11||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxviii, 11 and following, Jacob's dream at Bethel]; where we also read that he vowed to worship God with a special worship, saying: [[Gen 28:21|the Lord shall be my God|mihi Dominus in Deum]]. Now that is called holy which is set apart for divine worship.

paras.t: Quibus locutus es, pollicens, id est promittens, quod multiplicares semen eorum sicut stellas cœli, et sicut arenam quæ est in littore maris. Sic enim in Genesi Dominus Abrahæ loquitur : Suspice cœlum, et numera stellas, si potes : sic erit semen tuum. Insuper Jacob ait ad Dominum : Tu locutus es quod benefaceres mihi, et dilatares semen meum sicut arenam maris. Sed et Dominus ait Isaac : Multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas cœli. Fuit autem consuetudo populi Israelitici, in precibus suis memorari justitiæ Patriarcharum istorum, et divinarum promissionum eis factarum, ut Deus tam propter illorum virtutes ac merita, quam propter propriam veritatem, exaudiret ipsos orantes.
paras.en: [[3:36|To whom thou hast spoken, promising|Quibus locutus es, pollicens]], that is, making a promise, [[3:36|that thou wouldst multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is on the sea shore|quod multiplicares semen eorum sicut stellas cœli, et sicut arenam quæ est in littore maris]]. For so in Genesis the Lord speaks to Abraham: [[Gen 15:5|Look up to heaven and number the stars if thou canst|Suspice cœlum, et numera stellas, si potes]]: [[Gen 15:5|So shall thy seed be|sic erit semen tuum]]. Moreover Jacob says to the Lord: [[Gen 32:12|Thou didst say, that thou wouldst do well by me, and multiply my seed like the sand of the sea|Tu locutus es quod benefaceres mihi, et dilatares semen meum sicut arenam maris]]. And the Lord also says to Isaac: [[Gen 26:4|I will multiply thy seed like the stars of heaven|Multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas cœli]]. Now it was the custom of the people of Israel in their prayers to make mention of the righteousness of these Patriarchs and of the divine promises made to them, so that God, as much for their virtues and merits as for his own truthfulness, might hear them when they prayed.

paras.t: Quia, Domine, imminuti, id est numero pauciores effecti, sumus, plus quam omnes gentes : gladio enim, fame, peste, et captivitate pro maxima parte fuerunt Judæi consumpti tempore isto. Propter quod scriptum est in Baruch : Avertatur, Domine, ira tua, quia derelicti sumus pauci. Hoc quarto Regum et in Ezechiele plenius edocetur. Sic et Moyses pro tempore suo dixit ad populum Israel : Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris : non quia cunctas gentes numero vincebatis, quum sitis omnibus populis pauciores. Et sumus humiles, id est despecti et viles, in universa terra hodie propter peccata nostra : quia ubique a gentibus, inter quas erant dispersi et commorantes, despiciebantur. Quod propter sua patiebantur peccata, sicut per Jeremiam Deus frequenter eis prædixit : Dabo vos in commotionem et sibilum et maledictionem omnibus regnis terræ. Nam audientes famam calamitatis eorum, stupebant. Hinc dicit Baruch : Facti sumus subtus et non supra, quia peccavimus Domino Deo nostro.
paras.en: [[3:37|For we, O Lord, are diminished|Quia, Domine, imminuti]], that is, made fewer in number, [[3:37|more than any nation|plus quam omnes gentes]]: for at that time the Jews were for the most part consumed by sword, famine, pestilence and captivity. For this reason it is written in Baruch: [[Bar 2:13|Let thy wrath be turned away from us: for we are left a few|Avertatur, Domine, ira tua, quia derelicti sumus pauci]]. This is taught more fully in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 25:1||]] and in Ezechiel[[Ezech 12:16||]]. So too Moses, in his own time, said to the people of Israel: [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people|Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris]]: [[Deut 7:7|Not because you surpass all nations in number|non quia cunctas gentes numero vincebatis]], [[Deut 7:7|for you are the fewest of any people|quum sitis omnibus populis pauciores]]. [[3:37|and are brought low|Et sumus humiles]], that is, despised and vile, [[3:37|in all the earth this day for our sins|in universa terra hodie propter peccata nostra]]: because everywhere they were despised by the nations among whom they were scattered and dwelling. And they suffered this for their sins, as God often foretold to them through Jeremias: I will give you up to commotion, and to hissing, and to cursing, to all the kingdoms of the earth[[Jer 24:9||]][[Jer 25:18||]][[Jer 29:18||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiv, 17; xxv, 18; xxix, 18. Chapter xxiv has only ten verses (xxiv, 9 is probably meant); Denis gathers phrases from these places, and "commotion … to all the kingdoms of the earth" stands in Jer 34:17]. For those who heard the report of their calamity were astonished. Hence Baruch says: [[Bar 2:5|And we are brought under, and are not uppermost: because we have sinned against the Lord our God|Facti sumus subtus et non supra, quia peccavimus Domino Deo nostro]].

paras.t: Et non est in tempore hoc princeps, id est rex in populo Israel. Sedecias enim tunc captus asseritur. Et dux militiæ. Et Propheta, qui posset dare divinum responsum. Sed videtur contrarium : nam tempore isto in Chaldæa fuerunt Daniel atque Ezechiel, et alibi Jeremias. Ad quod dicendum opinor, quod Propheta hic dicitur ab actu prophetandi : et tempore isto non erat actualiter consolationem futuram divinitus nuntians. Neque holocaustum, id est oblatio quæ ad divinæ majestatis reverentiam totaliter comburebatur, significatque homines spirituales et viros perfectos, qui divino obsequio se integraliter mancipant, ac sanctæ caritatis igne penitus inflammantur. Neque sacrificium, neque oblatio. Secundum Albertum, sacrificium dicitur quod de liquidis vel aridis rebus fiebat; oblatio, quæ partim incendebatur, et partim reddebatur offerenti. Alii sacrificium exponunt esse quod partim incendebatur, partimque ad usum sacerdotum servabatur ; oblationem autem, quæ ex devotione offerebatur spontanea. Neque incensum, id est thymiama odoris, quod super altare thymiamatis offerebatur ad sacrificii consummationem, ut dicit Apostolus ad Hebræos. Neque locus primitiarum coram te, id est, in quo primitiæ frugum terræ Domino offerentur, quia Jerusalem et templum, ubi hæc secundum legem offerebantur, destructa fuerunt vel protinus destruenda. De his primitiis in Proverbiis Salomon monet : Honora Dominum de tua substantia, et de primitiis frugum tuarum.
paras.en: [[3:38|Neither is there at this time prince|Et non est in tempore hoc princeps]], that is, a king among the people of Israel; for Sedecias is said to have been taken captive at that time. [[3:38|or leader|Et dux]] of the army. [[3:38|or prophet|Et Propheta]], who could give an answer from God. But the contrary seems true: for at that time Daniel and Ezechiel were in Chaldea, and Jeremias elsewhere. To this I think it must be said that *prophet* is used here from the act of prophesying: and at that time there was no one actually announcing, from God, a consolation to come. [[3:38|or holocaust|Neque holocaustum]], that is, the offering that was wholly burnt in reverence of the divine majesty; and it signifies spiritual men and perfect men, who give themselves over entirely to the service of God, and are wholly inflamed with the fire of holy charity. [[3:38|or sacrifice, or oblation|Neque sacrificium, neque oblatio]]. According to Albert, a sacrifice is what was made of liquid or dry things; an oblation, what was partly burnt and partly given back to the offerer. Others explain that a sacrifice is what was partly burnt and partly kept for the use of the priests, and an oblation what was offered of spontaneous devotion. [[3:38|or incense|Neque incensum]], that is, the thymiama [the Greek word for incense] of sweet odour, which was offered upon the altar of incense for the completion of the sacrifice, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews[[Heb 9:6||]] [the margin gives Heb. ix, 6, where the priests are "accomplishing the offices of sacrifices"]. [[3:38|or place of first fruits before thee|Neque locus primitiarum coram te]], that is, in which the first fruits of the crops of the land were to be offered to the Lord: since Jerusalem and the temple, where these were offered according to the law, had been destroyed or were soon to be destroyed. Of these first fruits Solomon admonishes in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:9|Honour the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits|Honora Dominum de tua substantia, et de primitiis frugum tuarum]].

paras.t: Ut possimus invenire misericordiam tuam, id est tibi per talia exteriora secundum legem reconciliari, et pietatis tuæ consequi opem. Verumtamen talia exteriora non erant per se Deo accepta et placita, nec principaliter requisita, aut simpliciter necessaria ; sed primitiæ cordis quæ sunt præcipui fructus virtutum, devotio et pœnitentiæ actus, de quibus subjungitur.
paras.en: [[3:39|That we may find thy mercy|Ut possimus invenire misericordiam tuam]]: that is, be reconciled to thee through such outward things according to the law, and obtain the help of thy loving-kindness. Yet such outward things were not of themselves acceptable and pleasing to God, nor chiefly required, nor simply necessary; but the first fruits of the heart, which are the chief fruits of the virtues, devotion and acts of penance, of which he goes on to speak:

paras.t: Sed in anima contrita contritione pœnitentiali, id est se ipsam per illicitorum eradicationem et deplorationem conterente. Sicut enim corporaliter aliquid conteri dicitur, quando in minutissima frusta confringitur; sic anima spiritualiter conteri fertur, dum se ipsam a propria voluntate, concupiscentia, omnique culpa penitus exuit et confringit. Et spiritu humilitatis, id est spiritu nostro humiliante se ipsum, non alte, sed humiliter de se sentiendo ; vel, Spiritu humilitatis, id est in gratia Spiritus Sancti humilitatem donantis. Porro in homine anima et spiritus eamdem designant frequenter essentiam : quæ anima dicitur, in quantum corpus animat, format, vivificat ; et spiritus, quantum ad vires superiores, vel propter naturæ suæ simplicitatem : spiritus tamen multis modis in homine et in Scripturis accipitur. Suscipiamur ad veniam intra brachia tuæ clementiæ, ut scilicet per contritionem et humilitatem tibi reddamur accepti, juxta illud in Psalmo : Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus ; cor contritum et humiliatum, Deus, non despicies. Nempe per hæc duo peccator Deo præcipue reconciliatur, ut qui in vitiis delectatus est impie, et contra altitudinem Dei se pompose erexit, per pœnitentiam se affligens, dolens, ac divinæ se majestati profunde prosternens, contraria in se contrariis curet, sicque sanatus mente Deo salubriter vivat. Unde per Isaiam Dominus protestatur : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos? Et in Baruch asseritur : Anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, et oculi deficientes, dant gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino. Denique super illud Genesis, Isaac amabat Esau, ut Lyra allegat, Rabbi Moyses dicit : Dilectæ sunt magis tribulationes quam sacrificia. Sacrificia quippe sunt de divitiis hominis, tribulationes vero de corpore ejus, quod est carius sibi, secundum quod dicitur in Job : Pellem pro pelle, et cuncta quæ habet homo, dabit pro anima sua.
paras.en: [[3:39|nevertheless, in a contrite heart|Sed in anima contrita]] [Denis reads *in anima contrita*, "in a contrite soul", where the Vulgate has *in animo contrito*], contrite with penitential contrition: that is, a soul that crushes itself by rooting out and bewailing what is unlawful. For as something is said to be crushed bodily when it is broken into the smallest fragments, so the soul is said to be crushed spiritually when it wholly strips itself of, and breaks, its own will, concupiscence and every fault [*contritio*, from *conterere*, "to grind or crush to pieces"]. [[3:39|and humble spirit|Et spiritu humilitatis]] [literally "spirit of humility"], that is, by our spirit humbling itself, thinking of itself not loftily but humbly; or, *spirit of humility*, that is, in the grace of the Holy Spirit who gives humility. Now in man soul and spirit often designate the same essence: which is called soul inasmuch as it animates, forms and quickens the body, and spirit as regards the higher powers, or because of the simplicity of its nature; yet *spirit* is taken in many ways in man and in the Scriptures. [[3:39|let us be accepted|Suscipiamur]] to pardon within the arms of thy clemency: that is, so that through contrition and humility we may be made acceptable to thee; according to that word in the Psalm: [[Ps 50:19|A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.|Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus; cor contritum et humiliatum, Deus, non despicies.]] For by these two the sinner is chiefly reconciled to God: so that he who has taken wicked delight in vices, and has proudly lifted himself up against the loftiness of God, afflicting himself through penance, grieving, and prostrating himself deeply before the divine majesty, may cure contraries in himself by contraries, and so, healed in mind, may live to God unto salvation. Hence the Lord declares through Isaias: [[Is 66:2|But to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words?|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos?]] And in Baruch it is affirmed: [[Bar 2:18|But the soul that is sorrowful for the greatness of evil she hath done, and goeth bowed down, and feeble, and the eyes that fail|Anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, et oculi deficientes]], [[Bar 2:18|giveth glory and justice to thee the Lord|dant gloriam et justitiam tibi Domino]]. Moreover, on that word of Genesis, [[Gen 25:28|Isaac loved Esau|Isaac amabat Esau]], as Lyra reports, Rabbi Moses says: Tribulations are more beloved than sacrifices. For sacrifices come from a man's riches, but tribulations from his body, which is dearer to him; according to what is said in Job: [[Job 2:4|Skin for skin; and all that a man hath, he will give for his life|Pellem pro pelle, et cuncta quæ habet homo, dabit pro anima sua]].

paras.t: Sicut in holocausto arietum et taurorum, id est de istis animalibus facto, et sicut in millibus agnorum pinguium, sic fiat sacrificium nostrum hodie : id est, spirituale sacrificium cordis nostri, quo se tibi per contritionem et humilitatem sacrificat, præsentat et offert, sic et in tali fide ac devotione tibi hoc die atque in luce gratiæ seu sapientiæ atque clementiæ tuæ complaceat, in quali fide et devotione sacrificia illa legalia de agnis pinguibus ac ceteris animantibus facta, tibi complacuerunt, videlicet ex devotione et fide offerentium, non propria sua virtute. Propter quod dicunt theologi, quod sacrificia illa meritoria erant ex parte operis operantis, non operis operati. In conspectu tuo, id est coram pietatis tuæ respectu, ut nos clementer adspicias : juxta illud Psalmi, Oculi Domini super metuentes eum, et in eis qui sperant super misericordia ejus. Et in Genesi legitur : Respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus. Ut placeat tibi. Hoc semper permaxime optare debemus, ut opera nostra placeant Deo.
paras.en: [[3:40|As in holocausts of rams, and bullocks|Sicut in holocausto arietum et taurorum]], that is, made of these animals, [[3:40|and as in thousands of fat lambs|et sicut in millibus agnorum pinguium]], [[3:40|so let our sacrifice be made|sic fiat sacrificium nostrum]] [[3:40|this day|hodie]]: that is, may the spiritual sacrifice of our heart, by which it sacrifices, presents and offers itself to thee through contrition and humility, be pleasing to thee this day, and in the light of thy grace or wisdom and clemency, with such faith and devotion as those sacrifices of the law, made of fat lambs and other animals, were pleasing to thee: namely by the devotion and faith of the offerers, not by any power of their own. For this reason the theologians say that those sacrifices were meritorious on the part of the work of the one working, not of the work worked [that is, *ex opere operantis*, by the faith and devotion of the one offering, not *ex opere operato*, by the rite itself performed]. [[3:40|in thy sight|In conspectu tuo]], that is, before the regard of thy loving-kindness, that thou mayest look upon us with clemency; according to that word of the Psalm, [[Ps 32:18|the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: and on them that hope in his mercy|Oculi Domini super metuentes eum, et in eis qui sperant super misericordia ejus]]. And in Genesis we read: [[Gen 4:4|the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings|Respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus]]. [[3:40|that it may please thee|Ut placeat tibi]]. This we ought always most earnestly to desire: that our works may please God.

paras.t: Quoniam non est confusio confidentibus in te, id est, optato spei suæ bono non frustrantur, nec finaliter erubescent. Juxta hunc sensum ait Albertus : Confusio seu confundi, est a spe cadere, et rem speratam non invenire. Sic non est confusio speranti in Deo, quum ad Romanos dicat Apostolus : Spes non confundit. Et Psalmista : Sperantem autem in Domino misericordia circumdabit. In Ecclesiastico quoque habetur : Scitote, filii, quoniam nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est; permansit in mandatis ejus, et derelictus est. Præter hanc confusionis acceptionem, adhuc in Scripturis confusio duobus modis accipitur. Uno modo pro confusione bona, quæ est salubris erubescentia de peccato ad pœnitentiam aut salutem : et istam habent ad tempus sperantes in Domino, non tamen jugiter in mala conscientia habent eam coram ipso. Alia est confusio vitiosa, quo quis verecundatur sua fateri peccata, vel erubescit de his quæ non sunt veraciter inhonesta aut turpia, quamvis ipse ea quasi inhonesta aut turpia apprehendat : ut quum non volumus aliquid pro Deo pati, irrideri, aut pro nostris excessibus corripi. Ista in virtuosis locum non habet. Hinc scriptum est in Ecclesiastico : Pro anima tua non confundaris dicere verum : est enim confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam; non confundaris confiteri peccata tua. Interdum vero confusio sumitur pro vituperatione, reprobatione seu irrisione alicujus ab alio : et sic sancti et virtuosi dicuntur ab hominibus malis confundi. Quæ tamen non est vera et proprie dicta confusio, quia nec perfecti ex talibus intra se confunduntur, turbantur nec contristantur, sed potius in adversis exsultant, et bonæ conscientiæ testimonio eriguntur. Est autem confusio secundum æstimationem et apparentiam quamdam humanam : et secundum hunc modum Christus testatur in Psalmo ad Patrem, Tu scis improperium meum et confusionem meam, et reverentiam meam.
paras.en: [[3:40|for there is no confusion to them that trust in thee|Quoniam non est confusio confidentibus in te]]: that is, they are not cheated of the good their hope longed for, nor will they blush in the end. In this sense Albert says: Confusion, or being confounded, is to fall from hope and not to find the thing hoped for. Thus there is no confusion for one who hopes in God, since the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 5:5|hope confoundeth not|Spes non confundit]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 31:10|mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord|Sperantem autem in Domino misericordia circumdabit]]. In Ecclesiasticus too we have: [[Ecclus 2:11|know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded|Scitote, filii, quoniam nullus speravit in Domino, et confusus est]]; [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath continued in his commandment, and hath been forsaken?|permansit in mandatis ejus, et derelictus est]] [Denis leaves out "for who", so that "no one" carries over: no one has continued in his commandments and been forsaken]. Besides this meaning of confusion, confusion is taken in the Scriptures in two further ways. In one way, for good confusion, which is a wholesome blushing for sin, leading to penance or to salvation: and this those who hope in the Lord have for a time, yet they do not have it continually before him in an evil conscience. The other is vicious confusion, by which someone is ashamed to confess his sins, or blushes at things that are not truly dishonourable or shameful, though he himself takes them as dishonourable or shameful: as when we are unwilling to suffer anything for God, to be mocked, or to be rebuked for our excesses. This has no place in the virtuous. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 4:24|For thy soul be not ashamed to say the truth.|Pro anima tua non confundaris dicere verum]] [[Ecclus 4:25|For there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame that bringeth glory and grace.|est enim confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam]] [[Ecclus 4:31|Be not ashamed to confess thy sins|non confundaris confiteri peccata tua]] [the Douay-Rheims has "shame" and "ashamed" for *confusio* and *confundi*, "confusion" and "to be confounded"]. Sometimes, however, confusion is taken for the blame, reproof or mockery of someone by another: and in this way the saints and the virtuous are said to be confounded by evil men. Yet this is not true confusion, properly so called, since the perfect are not confounded within themselves by such things, nor troubled nor saddened, but rather exult in adversity, and are lifted up by the testimony of a good conscience. It is confusion, however, according to a certain human estimation and appearance: and in this way Christ testifies to the Father in the Psalm, [[Ps 68:20|Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, and my shame.|Tu scis improperium meum et confusionem meam, et reverentiam meam]]

paras.t: Et nunc, etiam in adversis et tribulationibus, sequimur te, id est, tuæ voluntati nos conformamus, et sensum tuum nostro præferimus, tibique obtemperamus, in toto corde nostro, scilicet in vi affectiva, intellectiva ac memorativa, totum nostrum velle, nosse et reminisci, ad tuam gloriam ordinando. In hoc nostra consistit perfectio. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico legitur : Gloria magna est sequi Dominum. Et Christus in Evangelio loquitur : Qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ. Job quoque dicit : Vestigia ejus secutus est pes meus. Hæc sequela spiritualis ac virtuosa est, ad felicitatem æternam tendens, qua non post concupiscentias proprias imus, sed Dei voluntatem implemus.
paras.en: [[3:41|And now|Et nunc]], even in adversities and tribulations, [[3:41|we follow thee|sequimur te]]: that is, we conform ourselves to thy will, and prefer thy mind to our own, and obey thee, [[3:41|with all our heart|in toto corde nostro]]: namely in the affective, the intellective and the memorative power, ordering all our willing, knowing and remembering to thy glory. In this our perfection consists. For this reason we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:38|It is great glory to follow the Lord|Gloria magna est sequi Dominum]]. And Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 8:12|He that followeth me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life|Qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ]]. Job too says: [[Job 23:11|My foot hath followed his steps|Vestigia ejus secutus est pes meus]].
