1.en: [[4:14|and the word|Et sermo]] [[4:14|of the holy ones|sanctorum]]: that is, of those on high who agree with the divine justice, it is the saying and the word that it be done so; [[4:14|and demand|et petitio]] of the same. For the saints demand vengeance against the wicked, and pray that God's almighty power be shown in the just casting down of the ungodly, according to that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 6:10|How long, O Lord (Holy and True), dost thou not judge and revenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?|Usquequo, Domine (sanctus et verus), non judicas, et non vindicas sanguinem nostrum de his qui sunt in terra]]

1.t: Donec cognoscant viventes in terra, quod dominetur Excelsus, id est Deus sublimis, in regno hominum, id est, cuncta regna ejus potestati subdantur : sicut plenius dictum est super illud, Ipse transfert regna atque constituit. Et cuicumque voluerit, dabit illud. Subest enim ei, quum voluerit, posse. Ideo secundum Dei voluntatem quisque ad præsidentiam est vocandus, ut ait Gregorius ; nec debet se quisquam ingerere, neque vulpinis uti cautelis, sed rem dispositioni divinæ committere, quum ad Hebræos dicat Apostolus : Nemo sumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron. Et humillimum hominem constituet super eum, id est super regni principatum. Quidam per humillimum hominem intelligunt Christum, qui protestatur, Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra ; alii, regem Nabuchodonosor, qui post suam amentiam profundissime humiliavit se Deo. Generalius tamen exponi potest indeterminate, quod Deus quemcumque hominem sibi placentem ad promovendum, promoveat ad regnandum, si ita decrevit, quantumcumque ille sit vilis atque abjectus. Juxta quod dicitur primo Regum libro : Suscitat de pulvere egenum, et de stercore elevat pauperem, ut sedeat cum principibus, et solium gloriæ teneat.
1.en: [[4:14|till the living know|Donec cognoscant viventes]] on earth, [[4:14|that the most High ruleth|quod dominetur Excelsus]], that is, God on high, [[4:14|in the kingdom of men|in regno hominum]], that is, that all kingdoms are subject to his power: as was said more fully on the words, He [[Dan 2:21|taketh away kingdoms, and establisheth them|transfert regna atque constituit]]. [[4:14|and he will give it to whomsoever it shall please him|Et cuicumque voluerit, dabit illud]]. For his power is at hand when he will[[Wis 12:18||]]. Therefore each man is to be called to high office according to God's will, as Gregory says; and no one ought to thrust himself forward, nor use the wiles of the fox, but commit the matter to the divine disposition, since the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 5:4|Neither doth any man take the honour to himself, but he that is called by God, as Aaron was|Nemo sumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron]]. [[4:14|and he will appoint the basest man over it|Et humillimum hominem constituet super eum]], that is, over the rule of the kingdom. Some understand by *the basest man* [that is, *humillimus*, the lowliest] Christ, who declares, [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]; others, King Nabuchodonosor, who after his madness humbled himself most deeply before God. But it can be explained more generally and without restriction: that God raises to reign any man whom it pleases him to raise, if he has so decreed, however mean and abject that man may be. According to what is said in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:8|He raiseth up the needy from the dust, and lifteth up the poor from the dunghill: that he may sit with princes, and hold the throne of glory|Suscitat de pulvere egenum, et de stercore elevat pauperem, ut sedeat cum principibus, et solium gloriæ teneat]].

1.t: Nunc visio tota exposita est ; subjungiturque consilium sancti Prophetæ, qui nil melius vidit pro rege, quam ad divinam confugere misericordissimam pietatem. Quamobrem, rex, consilium meum tibi placeat. Consilium etenim sapientium, præsertim in arduis, est quærendum atque servandum, ut in Tobia habetur : Consilium semper a sapiente perquire ; et in Proverbiis, Qui cuncta agunt consilio reguntur sapientia. Et peccata tua eleemosynis redime, ne debitor pœnæ permaneas, neque peccatis obnoxius, et iniquitates tuas misericordiis pauperum. Contraria enim curantur contrariis. Ideo decet, ut qui pauperes oppressisti, eis subvenias. Et ad impetrandum misericordiam Dei maxime confert, misericordiam pauperibus, imo et cunctis, impendere. Propter quod ait Salvator : Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Et iterum ait Scriptura : Sicut aqua exstinguit ignem, ita eleemosyna exstinguit peccatum ; et in Proverbiis, Per misericordiam et fidem purgantur peccata. Sed et in Tobia inde notabiliter scriptum est : Noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere : ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini. Eleemosyna ab omni peccato liberat, et non patietur animam ire in tenebras.
1.en: Now the whole vision has been explained; and there follows the counsel of the holy Prophet, who saw nothing better for the king than to take refuge in the most merciful divine goodness. [[4:24|Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to thee|Quamobrem, rex, consilium meum tibi placeat]]. For the counsel of the wise, especially in hard matters, is to be sought and kept, as is said in Tobias: [[Tob 4:19|Seek counsel always of a wise man|Consilium semper a sapiente perquire]]; and in Proverbs, [[Prov 13:10|they that do all things with counsel, are ruled by wisdom|Qui cuncta agunt consilio reguntur sapientia]]. [[4:24|and redeem thou thy sins with alms|Et peccata tua eleemosynis redime]], lest thou remain a debtor to punishment and liable for thy sins, [[4:24|and thy iniquities with works of mercy to the poor|et iniquitates tuas misericordiis pauperum]]. For contraries are cured by contraries [a maxim of the physicians, applied to the healing of the soul]. Therefore it is fitting that thou who hast oppressed the poor shouldst help them. And to obtain God's mercy it avails most to show mercy to the poor, nay, to all. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]]. And again Scripture says: As water quencheth fire, so alms quencheth sin[[Ecclus 3:33||]] [the margin notes "according to the old version", that is, an older Latin rendering; the Vulgate reads: Water quencheth a flaming fire, and alms resisteth sins]; and in Proverbs, [[Prov 15:27|By mercy and faith sins are purged away|Per misericordiam et fidem purgantur peccata]]. And in Tobias too it is notably written on this: [[Tob 4:7|turn not away thy face from any poor person: for so it shall come to pass that the face of the Lord shall not be turned from thee|Noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere : ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini]]. [[Tob 4:11|alms deliver from all sin|Eleemosyna ab omni peccato liberat]], [[Tob 4:11|and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness|et non patietur animam ire in tenebras]].
